params.message: steps up to the ATM terminal and makes a deposit.

chitchat: Thea pulls a shot for nobody, tastes it off the back of a spoon, and tips it away.
"Board four has been the same position for two days. They come up, they look at it, they go home."
The lever comes down with a sound like a door closing somewhere expensive.
"Rain's coming in over the yards. You get about nine minutes' warning from up here."
description: A composed woman in her fifties working a sixty-year-old lever machine with the unhurried economy of somebody who has never once had to rush it. She wears the counter like a uniform and the view like it's nothing. She knows which chair every regular takes and what they drink, and she has never written either down.

board.text: "Sit at one. That's all it takes — nobody's going to ask if you're any good." She nods at the window side. "Mr Ferro comes up most days and Miss Krebs when she's speaking to him. If a board's got somebody at it and an empty chair opposite, that chair is an invitation. That's the whole etiquette of the room."

bye.text: "Mm." She's already wiping down the group head. The city goes on doing whatever it does out there.

gossip.text: Thea considers you for a moment longer than is comfortable. "People talk over a board like the person pouring is part of the furniture. Eighteen years of it." She sets the cloth down. "Here's one that's gone cold enough to repeat."

root.familiar: "Yours is coming." The lever is already down. She doesn't look up. "Board by the glass is free, if you're playing. I kept it free."
root.first: The woman behind the counter watches you take in the window first, the way everyone does. "They all look at the city," she says. "Give it a week and you'll look at the boards instead." She sets a cup down on the marble without being asked. "Thea Wrenn. I've been up here eighteen years. Coffee's eighteen credits and worth it once."
root.known: "Back, then." Thea reaches for a cup before you've said anything. "Same as last time, or are we being adventurous?"
root.text: Thea has the lever half-down before you've finished crossing the carpet. "Morning. Blend's the blend, the boards are free, and the glass gets cleaned Thursdays." A pause, dry. "Everything else up here you have to ask for."

roast.text: "Beans that grew in dirt, on a hillside, under weather." She lets that sit. "There are four places left doing that and I am not going to tell you which one sells to me. Everything downstairs is grown in a tray under a lamp, and it tastes like a tray under a lamp." The lever comes down. "That's the whole secret. It's not a good secret, it's just expensive."

view.text: "Best in the building, and I'll fight the Sky Deck about it." She tips her head at the glass. "Forty floors up you're above it. Eighteen, you're still *in* it — you can see which windows are lit and which stairwell somebody's running down. Close enough to be a city. Far enough to be quiet." She shrugs. "Forty floors is a postcard."

clothing_layers: a long charcoal apron over a pressed white shirt, sleeves turned back twice
dark wool trousers and flat leather shoes worn soft

name: Thea Wrenn
